summary: 1909 wooden light and fog-signal station on a Mendocino headland, built for the lumber schooners; the lens turns again and the keepers houses are rented out.

lens.where: lantern room of the lighthouse (Chance Brothers, England)

structures.note: Attached to the east end of the fog-signal building; 47 ft (NRHP)
Two 18-hp engines drove an air compressor for twin sirens (Friends)
Listed as installed in the 1921 Commissioner report; USLHS says post-1909

staffing.note: Last civilian keeper retired in 1963; Coast Guard manned the station until the 1970s (Friends)

access.note: State historic park; grounds open sunrise to sunset; lighthouse open 11 a.m. to 4 p.m. with lens tours to the lantern on set days; half-mile walk from parking

stay.note: Keepers houses rented as vacation homes (keepers association)

facts.agency: California State Parks; managed with Point Cabrillo Light Station (keepers association)

events.note: Keepers dwellings completed (USLHS: 1908); contract accepted later in 1908 (Friends)
Tower and fog-signal building completed; station finished 10 June 1909 (Friends, NRHP)
Lit 10 June 1909 under head keeper Wilhelm Baumgartner
Third-order Fresnel lens by Chance Brothers, England
Steam-powered compressors feeding twin sirens (Friends)
Oil lamp upgraded to oil-vapor lamp (Friends)
Electricity reaches the station (keepers association, Friends)
Clockwork replaced by an electric motor (keepers association; Friends gives 1935 for motors)
Lighthouse Service absorbed into the Coast Guard
February 1960 storm: erosion, waves over the lighthouse, fog-signal building damaged
Last civilian keeper William Owens retires, 28 February 1963 (Friends)
Coast Guard announced plan to remove the lens to a Virginia museum; public outcry kept it in place
California State Coastal Conservancy purchases the station (Friends; keepers association gives 1992 for possession)
Major restoration begins with the blacksmith shop and oil house
Lens removed for cleaning in August; lantern room lifted off by crane in November
Restored lantern room and lens replaced and the lens lit again in spring 1999 (Friends)
California State Parks purchases the station for four million dollars (Friends)
Easternmost keepers dwelling restored and opened as a museum (Friends)
Head keepers dwelling opens as the Lighthouse Inn (Friends); inn ran until early 2010
Lens stopped on 29 December 2022 when its 1937 motor burned out (Friends)
Surge of water floods the lighthouse with two feet of water, 5 January 2023 (Friends)
Lens restarted 2 October 2023 after the Coast Guard rebuilt its motor (Friends)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The keepers association says the point was surveyed in 1873 but construction began in 1908; Congress authorized the money in 1906, and the station was first lit in 1909. The 1873 survey is the earliest date and not a build date.
Friends dates the Conservancy purchase to 1991; the keepers association dates the Conservancy taking possession to 1992. Both are recorded; the purchase and the handover may differ.

notes_for_editor: Roster is the USLHS archive as printed by roster.py (44 lines, 1909-1969); the Coast Guard lines carry no rank. Lines named only in the archive and LF are kept as printed. Post-1960 names appear only as the archive prints them, with no personal detail. Conflicts: (1) NRHP last paragraph says 'Since its establishment in 1875' while its own text and every other source give 1909 (keepers association: surveyed 1873); read as a drafting slip, not used. (2) NRHP calls the fog-signal building one-story; LF says one-and-a-half-story. Story uses the NRHP wording. (3) Motor: keepers association 1937, LF 1935 (LF says electric motors came with electricity). (4) Conservancy: LF 1991 purchase; keepers association 1992 possession. (5) Visiting: State Parks page (checked 22 Oct 2026) and keepers home page say open daily 11-4 with lens tours on set days; LF (older notes) says the tower opens only a few days a year. (6) Record range_nm 22.0 vs keepers association 'range of 13-15 miles'; not changed here. Record structure height 14.0 m vs NRHP/LF 47 ft (14.3 m). (7) Names: LF spells O'Neill, Kennet H. Ferrell and James A. Taylor and Thomas Allen Atkinson; USLHS forms kept, variants in note. (8) Baumgartner's St. George Reef service, the 1904 Board request, the Frolic wreck, the 1960 storm account and Cora Owens's goat are from LighthouseFriends alone; LF prints Cora Owens's account from the Keeper's Log (Spring 1990), which was not read directly. (9) Commissioner 1921 entry (water tank $1,031) is OCR'd; the printed page is not confirmed (scan p. 660 cited); the page image should be checked. (10) The 1913 commendation was read from the Bulletin text (OCR 'fog signa l'); quote avoids the broken word. (11) The SF Call notice is OCR text read through newspapers.py. (12) No Lighthouse Board report for 1904-1910 is in the corpus; the 1904 request is cited to LF only. (13) Keepers' association says Baumgartner invited residents of Pine Grove; LF says neighbors near the station; both are cited. (14) Newspaper search for other Point Cabrillo mentions returned only 1909 notice and 1912 steamer mention; no 1923 or 1960 newspaper text was found. Story (h3 pass 2026-10-22 resume): Lighthouse Friends describes the fog-signal building as one-and-a-half-story and the NRHP as one-story; the story says only "a fog-signal building". Friends gives electric motors for the lens and diaphone in 1935; the keepers association gives the clockwork replacement in 1937; both are stated. Cora Owens's own 1960 storm account is printed on the Friends page, but the printed block is not in the cached text, so the story uses only Friends's narrative and the goat account, which the cached text does include. The 1904 request is quoted as the Board asked for "a light and fog-signal" (Friends).
